title: CI Build Server Out of Disk Space
intro: Every build on the shared CI runner just started failing with 'no space left on device'. Nobody changed the pipeline config.

steps.prompt: Confirm the disk is actually full at the host level first.
steps.fake_output:
Filesystem      Size  Used  Avail  Use%  Mounted on
/dev/sda1       100G   99G   1.0G   99%  /
steps.hint: Start broad — confirm the symptom before narrowing down what's causing it.

steps.prompt: Check whether Docker specifically is what's eating the space.
steps.fake_output:
TYPE            TOTAL   ACTIVE   SIZE      RECLAIMABLE
Images          340     2        71.2GB    70.8GB (99%)
Containers      512     0        8.1GB     8.1GB (100%)
Build Cache     -       -        12.4GB    12.4GB
steps.hint: docker system df breaks Docker's own disk usage down by category.

steps.prompt: 340 images, 512 stopped containers, all left over from months of CI builds that never cleaned up. Reclaim everything unused, including build cache.
steps.fake_output:
Deleted Containers: 512
Deleted Images: 338
Deleted build cache objects: 1204
Total reclaimed space: 90.3GB
steps.hint: -a is needed here since most of the space is in tagged-but-unused images, not just dangling ones.

steps.fake_output:
Filesystem      Size  Used  Avail  Use%  Mounted on
/dev/sda1       100G    9G   91G    9%   /
steps.hint: Always confirm a fix actually worked rather than assuming the prune command succeeded as expected.

resolution: The CI runner had been building a fresh image (and leaving behind a stopped container) on every single pipeline run for months, with nothing ever cleaning them up — Docker never removes old images, containers, or build cache on its own. It hit 99% and every subsequent build failed. The immediate fix was a full prune; the real fix is adding a scheduled 'docker system prune -a -f --filter until=24h' job to the runner (or configuring the CI system's own cleanup), so this doesn't silently accumulate back to 100% in another few months.
